correctness.rationale: Every residue modulo a has an exact Apéry threshold. The proof calculates the threshold for r=dj and r=dj+s, isolates one suffix gap of each long length dj, and counts each shorter length via t+1 consecutive threshold rows in each of t interior intervals, with a separate boundary count for length d−1. Symmetry yields reflected blocks of represented integers, while Q=(1−x)sum_{n in S}x^n makes exponent differences precisely the run lengths. All hypotheses and boundaries d,t>=2, the last gap, and d=2 are handled. Exact DP, an independent Apéry oracle, and independent explicit enumeration agree in 165 parameter cases, encompassing 1,058,035 integer membership checks; the infinite proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: Complete per-length multiplicities address an explicit mathematical gap in recent cyclotomic/semigroup literature, which had classified allowed gap lengths generally and counted frequencies only in ±1 residues. The two-parameter family b mod a=d occupies distinct nontrivial residues; the uniform multiplicity and separated long gap spectrum are evaluated exactly for all parameters. It yields the exact nonzero coefficient count and includes actual binary cyclotomic instances (e.g. a=13,b=17). This is a nontrivial structural frequency law, not merely a genus or maximum-gap recomputation.
